newsitem.title: FRANCE: French speaker wants to rebuild Franco-German ties.
newsitem.headline: French speaker wants to rebuild Franco-German ties.

text.p: France's National Assembly speaker Laurent Fabius on Tuesday urged the heads of the German and French governments to address each other's parliaments in order to revive a friendship soured by differences over the single European currency.

Fabius, a former Socialist premier, told a seminar on Franco-German relations that Chancellor Helmut Kohl should address the French National Assembly and French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin the Bundestag in an effort to restore frayed ties.

He said the Franco-German pairing, which has been the driving force of European unity, was going through "very serious difficulties" following last month's bilateral summit in the French town of Poitiers and a European Union summit in Amsterdam.
"This is a serious and unprecedented situation that (former European Commission president) Jacques Delors rightly described as a fiasco," he said.
"In order to emerge from this spiral of misunderstanding, the first thing to do is to repair the frayed threads at the top," Fabius said.
"Let (Kohl and Jospin) explain themselves and learn to know each other better," he said.
The two countries are at odds over calls by France's new left-wing government for a political counterweight to the European Central Bank and for EU policies to create jobs.
Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said last week that economic and monetary union (EMU) was hanging in the balance because of "fundamental dissent" between Paris and Bonn.

"Too much is at stake in the Franco-German relationship for it to be taken for granted, as it is going through serious problems that are increasingly apparent despite ritual meetings between the two countries' leaders," Fabius said.
"All of Europe's great successes were achieved thanks to (Franco-German) coordination. Conversely, many of the failures were due to lack of consultation with Germany," he said.
